steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray, and place squash halves cut-side down on the sheet. Bake until squash is tender but still crunchy, about 40 minutes. Set aside to cool.
Once cool enough to handle, shred squash flesh from rind using a fork. Set aside.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and garlic in butter until soft. Add squash to the skillet, and cook until hot. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Spaghetti Squash Saute
raw_recipe.description: This simple side dish made with spaghetti squash, onion, and garlic can be served with just about anything.

review.reviewBody: I grow my own spaghetti squash and cannot say enough about this wonderful veggie! FYI...to speed up the process with no change to the taste or texture, use the MICROWAVE!!! a nice medium (typical) sized squash takes about 10 mins on high in a shallow baking dish with a small amount of water and salt to create steam. follow same steps as in this recipe just use your microwave. Also, be adventurous, this squash is fabulous with butter and dried italian herbs, or drizzled with rosemary infused olive oil (a cinch to make) if it sounds good on pasta it will be great with this squash!

Very simple yet tasty and with a surprising texture. I added two variants: added 1/2 cup of white wine for flavor at the end of the sautéing process (make sure it is all evaporated before serving) - I used some weeks-old leftovers of Gewurtztraminer; and I cooked the squash in a grill, over a cast iron griddle for 30 minutes keeping the temperature between 400 and 450F. It was a very successful side with grilled salmon - even picky kids went for seconds

The first change to the recipe was to saute some chopped grape tomatoes and fresh spinach into the onion and garlic (I used 6 cloves of garlic). I added a 1/4 cup jar parmesan cheese to the pan (when the squash was placed in after roasting) and sprinkled in some dried italian seasoning and parsley. I chopped some fresh oregano into the pan. Let all the flavors cook through for a few seconds and enjoy! Delicious!

Very good! To save time, I was planning to microwave the squash. Then I read the top reviewers' comments, and that's what she did! My squash was small to medium in size, and after poking multiple holes with a knife, I microwaved it about 13 min. Ten minutes should do it. Had to wait 25 min just to slice it because it was so hot. Carefully removed the seeds, and with a fork, got the strands from the squash. The salt and pepper are really needed for flavor; I also added some fresh parsley. I had half of it for a one-bowl meal. Will have the other half another time.
Simple and easy to make. I used olive oil to it healthier in place of the butter and simply sauteed the squash over a low fire till golden brown without roasting.

I made this with exception I did not have feta cheese on hand so I substituted Parmesan and a shredded Jack/Cheddar combo cheese. Turned out great. Can use for a vegetable dish either main or side course. I found that I needed to cook the squash for 50 minutes at 350°F.

I loved how easy this was to just put it in the crock pot and forget it. The skin was very easy to cut when it was all cooked and easy to scoop out the seeds. I just added salt, pepper and butter and loved it. I did mine for 6 hours with a liner in my crock.

My husband and I are exploring different foods and neither of us have ever had spaghetti squash and this recipe and cooking guide was superb! I did use the microwave to reduce cooking time as suggested in another review using a small amount of water and sprinkle of salt in a shallow cooking container, halving lengthwise and placing upside down, microwaving on high for 15 minutes. I work all day and needed to speed up the prep time, lol. After preparing as suggested, we served this like pasta under chicken Marsala. Mmmmmm soooo good! Thank you for the recipe and suggestions from other reviews!

This is pretty good. I did cut the butter to 3TB as my squash was small. Next time I will likely cut the butter again- probably to 2 TB just to cut the calories. It had good flavor but somewhat bland as stated. I added basil to the squash before cooking and that added a nice touch. Quick and easy!
So easy and very good. I cook my squash in the microwave - cut in half , remove the seeds, rub the squash with olive oil and add salt and pepper. Cook 5 -10 minutes depending on the size.

This is easy and delicious. The first time I made it, I followed directions exactly and ended up with "mush" LOL but the 2nd time it was perfect. I poke holes all over the squash and nuke for 4-5 minutes before trying to cut in half- makes it so much easier. Just keep that in mind when you bake it- you've already cooked it for 5 minutes so 40 minutes is 5 minutes too long (plus you add it to the onions and garlic and saute it). I have yet another squash waiting to be cooked tonight... thanks for this great side dish!
This was really good. I added parmesan cheese and italian seasoning. The spaghetti squash took longer than listed and I had to throw it in the microwave to finish cooking it. Will make again!
Use your instant pot to cook it then you can do the sautéing when you are ready. Instant pot is 9 minutes.

This was my first time making spaghetti squash and it came out wonderful! I didn't add the onion as my sister doesn't like them and instead added spinach, which was a great mix. It didn't take 48 hours for the two of us to finish this.
It's easy and delicious! I microwave the squash. I add 1 tbsp butter and tbsp olive oil instead of 1/4 c butter to cut down on the fat.
We really liked this. I used green onions instead of cooking onion. It did need more seasoning. I used garlic pepper and organic no-salt seasoning. But taste and season as your family likes.
EXCELLENT! I used miyokos vegan butter as a sub-wow! I’ll be making this again quite a bit
It was so good! I followed the recipe exactly and it came out great. I will definitely be having it again.

Super super yummy! For once I wanted spaghetti squash without the spaghetti sauce, and this was delish. I melted a little more butter because we love butter and I sprinkled some dried basil on top, maybe 1/2 tsp. Very very good.
Simple and good!!!
